name: ink-arrow
title: Ink Arrow
description: A hand-drawn arrow that draws itself from one point to another in stop-motion poses.
useWhen: A hand-drawn annotation should point from one thing to another: callouts over paper or scrapbook scenes.
The pointing itself is part of the story and should be seen being drawn, pose by pose.
avoidWhen: You need a straight technical connector or a diagram edge: this is a wobbly pen line with a personality.
The arrow must follow another element's live position: the endpoints are fixed in the layout.
author: Remocn

variables.label: Card title
variables.description: Large line on the card the arrow points at.

variables.label: Card subtitle
variables.default: Positioned by you, drawn by the pen

variables.label: Curvature
variables.description: How much the shaft bows; negative bends the other way.

variables.label: Opening pressure
variables.description: Stroke width at the start, as a fraction of the brush width.

variables.label: Closing pressure
variables.description: Stroke width at the end, as a fraction of the brush width.

variables.label: Grain
variables.description: How rough the ink edge is.

variables.label: Head size
variables.description: Length of the arrow head strokes.

variables.label: Draw frames
variables.description: Frames (30 fps) the shaft takes to draw.

variables.label: Head frames
variables.description: Frames (30 fps) the arrow head takes to draw.

variables.label: Frames per pose
variables.description: How many frames each drawing pose is held.
